description: Kanhe protocol objects added in specification revision v0.8 (requests and answers), built by an independent Python encoder from spec/kanhe.cddl and run by the reference interpreter tools/testvectors/wasm_ref.py. The requesting contract (request_contract in tools/testvectors/test_contracts.py, interface `interface`) writes byte-string arguments as its output, aborts with text arguments, makes one request {1: kind, 2: params, 3: time + after, 4: "result"} per [kind, params, after] in array arguments, and otherwise makes none; for an answer (input key 9) its state becomes [status, request] and it records the event [done|failed|expired, kind]; otherwise the state stays (null for a creation). A clerk (a person), a notice agent (an AI agent under the clerk; scope keys 8 [result] and 9 [notify]), a panel executor (a device; keys 8 [result] and 9 [invoice, provision, reclaim, suspend]), a billing executor (under the panel executor; key 9 [invoice]), and a keeper (key 8 [result, when.due]) call five instances: a service whose requests are answered done, failed, and expired, on time and late, with two left open, one overdue; a final instance that takes answers; one at the limit of 64 open requests; one that tries what a request may be; and one whose creation makes a request and a part. Each statement registers at its `registered_at` (the log entries carry it); refused statements either break the CDDL (`malformed`) or are validated against the state after the first `after` statements, at `at`; `why` names the rule (answered, early, answer function, consents, no such request, other instance, final, head, authority, narrowing, deadline, reply, open) or `contract` when the contract's run refuses it (its run says how). `runs` lists every contract run: the input the home builds (key 9 for an answer), and the outcome, output, fuel, and verdict. `requests` lists every request: its id, HASH(["request", call, position]), its instance, the requesting call's index and statement id, its position, kind, params (encoded), deadline, reply, the time it was asked at, and its answer (status, index, time, and how late), and whether it is overdue at the checkpoint. `instances` gives each instance's final state, status, parties, head, finality, history, depth, parent, and its open requests. `disclosures` holds outside responses an executor kept, with their salts and HASH(salt || response), which answers carry. `log_entries` holds the whole log, ending with the state commitment over `state_leaves`; `checkpoint` (signed at `checkpoint_time`) covers it. `evidence` holds signed contract evidence for three instances (as in protocol-v0.7.json: entries, involved objects, consent pins) and what a report shows: per call, the requests it made and its answer (request, status, lateness, actor, signer, delegation); the instance's requests, the open ones, and those overdue at the checkpoint. `contract_checks` counts the inputs on which the contract agreed with an independent model. Signatures are Ed25519 (deterministic); keys are throwaway: seed = SHA-256("Kanhe test key: <name>"), and for the customer's ledger "Customer root" and "Customer log".

the agent reports the notice failed, and asks again
the billing executor reports the invoice issued
the keeper fires a rule that asks for a suspension
the keeper expires the second notice
the panel executor reports the suspension, late
open a second service
end it, asking for its address to be reclaimed and a notice

open a third service
ask for 16 requests (1 of 4)
ask for 16 requests (2 of 4)
ask for 16 requests (3 of 4)
ask for 16 requests (4 of 4)
answer a request at the limit, asking one more
open a fourth service
ask at the limits: the earliest and latest deadlines, a kind of 64 bytes, params of 4,096 bytes, another reply
answer it with its reply
open a fifth service with a part, asking for a notice
ask on the part
the panel executor provisions the part
ask for an address to be reclaimed within the hour, and a review
the clerk answers the review by hand
